name: St Mark’s Basilica
places: Horses of St Mark, St Mark’s Basilica
description: Venice’s great square and the gold-mosaic basilica at its end, home of the bronze horses of St Mark and the Tetrarchs sculpture.

name: Doge’s Palace
places: Doge’s Palace and the Piombi prison cells
Hall of the Great Council, Doge’s Palace
description: The Gothic palace that ran the Venetian republic, with the vast Great Council hall, the Piombi prison cells and the Bridge of Sighs.

name: Rialto Bridge
description: The oldest bridge across the Grand Canal, a 16th-century stone arch lined with shops, next to the Rialto market.

name: La Fenice
description: Venice’s opera house, burned down and rebuilt more than once, most recently reopening in 2003. You can tour it by day.

name: Grand Hotel des Bains
places: Grand Hotel des Bains, Lido di Venezia
description: A Belle Époque beach hotel on the Lido, the setting of Thomas Mann’s Death in Venice. It has been closed since 2010.

name: Jewish Ghetto
places: Campo del Ghetto Nuovo, Jewish Ghetto
Jewish Ghetto, Campo del Ghetto Nuovo
description: The main square of the Ghetto, set up in 1516 and the origin of the word “ghetto”, with old synagogues and the Jewish Museum.

name: Corte del Milion
places: Corte del Milion, Marco Polo’s family home
description: A small courtyard near the Rialto where Marco Polo’s family lived. Their house later burned down, and a theatre now stands on the site.

name: Gallerie dell’Accademia
description: The city’s main collection of Venetian painting from the 1300s to the 1700s: Bellini, Giorgione, Titian, Tintoretto and Veronese.

name: Scuola Grande di San Rocco
description: A confraternity’s meeting house whose walls and ceilings are covered with more than 50 paintings by Tintoretto.

name: Frari church
places: Frari church (Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari)
description: A huge Gothic friars’ church with Titian’s Assumption over the high altar and the tombs of Titian and the composer Monteverdi.

name: San Barnaba
description: An 18th-century church and the canal-side square in front of it, in Dorsoduro. The church was a library in Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.

name: La Pietà church
places: La Pietà church, Riva degli Schiavoni
description: The waterfront church of the orphanage where Vivaldi taught music, rebuilt after his death. It still hosts concerts.

name: Scuola Grande di San Marco
places: Ospedale Civile city hospital, Scuola Grande di San Marco
description: A Renaissance confraternity building with a marble trompe-l’œil façade, now the entrance to the city hospital and a museum of medical history.

name: Naval History Museum
places: Museo Storico Navale, naval history museum
description: A museum near the Arsenal on Venice’s life at sea, with ship models, weapons and a model of the doge’s ceremonial barge.

name: Arsenal gate
description: The Renaissance land gate of the Arsenal, the vast state shipyard that built Venice’s fleet, guarded by stone lions brought from Greece.

name: Torcello Cathedral
description: A cathedral founded in 639 on a now nearly empty island in the northern lagoon, with Byzantine mosaics including a huge Last Judgement.
